sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was cyclical rather than smooth: a 22.4% fall in FY2020 to $41.7 billion was followed by a 22.1% rebound in FY2021 to $51.0 billion [F5][D198][F6][D251].
The FY2020 decline came from lower sales volume driven by lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].
FY2023 was the margin peak, with operating margin up 6.0pp to 19.3% on favorable price realization and higher sales volume [F28][D370][P31].
FY2025 revenue rose 4.3% to $67.6 billion on higher sales volume, partly offset by unfavorable price realization [F10][D463][P13].
Power & Energy is now the largest segment at 47.6% of revenue in FY2025, up from 41.8% in FY2023 [D757][D753].
Power & Energy grew 11.6% in FY2025 and contributed 5.2pp of the 4.3% total growth, while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D758][D759][D463][D765][D766].
Within Power & Energy, Power Generation sales rose 32.5% and added 3.9pp, the single largest driver [D894][D895].
Construction Industries' decline came from unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher sales volume [P8].
Operating income fell 14.7% in FY2025 against 4.3% revenue growth, so there was no operating leverage [F20][D464][D463].
Operating margin was 16.5% in FY2025, above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [F30][D1123][F29][D1122].
Cost of revenue added 4.2pp of margin pressure in FY2025, rising 11.3% against 4.3% revenue growth, within a 3.7pp operating-margin decline [D490][D478][D463][D476].

Operating profit fell $1.921 billion, primarily on unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion and unfavorable price realization of $817 million, with manufacturing costs largely reflecting higher tariffs [P9].
Net margin fell 3.5pp to 13.1%, and the 24.0% effective tax rate was above the 19.7% of FY2024 [F50][D477][D449][D396].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025, above the 1.13x of FY2019 [F80][F40][D450][D132].
Free cash flow fell 11.2% to $8.9 billion, a 13.2% margin against a 11.9% window median [F100][D469][D447][D1129].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion, lifting capex to 1.25x D&A from 0.92x, as the 10-K cites an increase in capital expenditures [F90][D470][D452][D399][P3].
Machinery operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes, partly offset by lower profit before taxes [P4].
Net debt widened to $26.2 billion in FY2025 from $24.9 billion, as total debt grew 14.1% and cash rose 44.9% [D456][D403][D485][D484].
Net cash was -38.8% of revenue, a 43rd percentile rank against seven industrials peers whose median was -35.6% [D457][D1151][D1152].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion plus dividends of $2.7 billion were 89.0% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [X140][X150][D458][D459][D483].
Return on average equity was 43.5%, in the 100th percentile against six peers whose median was 23.3% [D462][D1155][D1156].
Net cash has fallen for two straight years, from -$22.1 billion in FY2023 to -$26.2 billion in FY2025, as debt rose while cash stayed flat [D350][D403][D456].
Revenue declined 3.4% in FY2024 to $64.8 billion, the only down year since FY2020 [F9][D410].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy statement and differs from the 10-K by up to 0.06%, so the 10-K figures should be used where precision matters [R3][F40][X20].
Segment revenue members on one axis sum to 219% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so they must not be added together [R6].
Operating margin: a FY2026 print below the 14.3% window median would confirm the FY2025 erosion, while a return above the 20.2% FY2024 high would reverse it [D1123][D1122].
Capex: FY2025 reached 4.2% of revenue against a 2.9% FY2016 level; a further rise above 4.2% would keep free cash flow margin below its 11.9% median [D446][D6][D1129].
Net cash: a third year of decline below -$26.2 billion would extend the leverage trend, while a move back toward the -$22.1 billion FY2023 level would reverse it [D456][D350].
